claim: During cell division, the spontaneous mutation rate is expressed as the probability of mutations per generation.
source: During cell division, the spontaneous mutation rate is expressed as the probability of mutations per generation (Luria and Delbrück, 1943; Lea and Coulson, 1949)
evidence: Supported by citations to foundational work by Luria and Delbrück (1943) and Lea and Coulson (1949)

claim: During quiescence, the spontaneous mutation rate is expressed per unit of time.
source: whereas during quiescence it will be expressed per unit of time.
evidence: Stated as a contrast to the replication-dependent mutation rate, based on logical inference about non-dividing cells

claim: During quiescence, the unicellular haploid fission yeast accumulates mutations as a linear function of time.

claim: The mutational landscape of quiescence is characterized by insertion/deletion (indels) accumulating as fast as single nucleotide variants (SNVs).

claim: The mutational landscape of quiescence is characterized by elevated amounts of deletions.

claim: The replication-independent mutational spectrum at the whole-genome level was confirmed in a clonally aged population after 3 months of quiescence.

claim: Genomes continuously evolve under two alternating phases (growth and quiescence) that impact their size and composition.

source: The genetics of quiescence underscores the importance of a time-dependent process (Goldmann et al., 2016; Hazen et al., 2016; Kumar and Subramanian, 2002; Ségurel et al., 2014) to the overall mutation spectrum.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion supported by multiple citations

claim: The time-dependent process should help to fine-tune the accuracy of the 'molecular clock' that measures the evolutionary distance of two closely related species with their common ancestor.
source: This time-dependent process should also help to fine-tune the accuracy of the 'molecular clock' that measures, in units of time (dos Reis et al., 2016), the evolutionary distance of two closely related species with their common ancestor.
evidence: Stated as a speculation about implications for molecular clock accuracy

claim: The viability at 3 months of quiescence is about 0.05%.
source: In these conditions, the viability at 3 months is about 0.05% (Figure 4).
evidence: Stated as an observation, supported by data in Figure 4

claim: A biphasic viability curve was observed, with a cell death acceleration after three weeks of quiescence.
source: From several experiments, we observed a biphasic viability curve, with a cell death acceleration after three weeks of quiescence (Figure 4).
evidence: Stated as an observation, supported by data in Figure 4

claim: No phenotypes were observed upon examination of 384 colonies after 1 day or 1 month of quiescence.
source: We did not observe any phenotype upon examination of 384 colonies after 1 day or 1 month of quiescence.
evidence: Stated as an observation from phenotypic survey, shown in Table 6

claim: After 2 and 3 months of quiescence, 4/376 (1.1%) and 6/334 (1.8%) colonies displayed phenotypes, respectively.
source: However, after 2 and 3 months, we observed 4/376 (1.1%) and 6/334 (1.8%) colonies displaying phenotypes (Table 6), respectively.
evidence: Stated as an observation from phenotypic survey, shown in Table 6

claim: Genetic crosses confirmed that the phenotype observed in the 10 colonies derives from a single mutated locus.
source: Genetic crosses confirmed that the phenotype observed in the 10 colonies derives from a single mutated locus.
evidence: Stated as an observation from genetic analysis

claim: Mutations were found mapping to alg5, alg8, aur1, ccc2, gdi1 and oca8 genes in six strains isolated after three months.
source: We sequenced the genomes of the six strains isolated after three months and found mutations mapping to alg5, alg8, aur1, ccc2, gdi1 and oca8 genes.
evidence: Stated as an observation from whole-genome sequencing

claim: The genes alg5, alg8, aur1, ccc2, gdi1 and oca8 encode for cell wall and vacuole/membrane trafficking functions that might improve viability during quiescence.
source: These genes encode for cell wall and vacuole/membrane trafficking functions that might improve viability during quiescence.
evidence: Stated as an inference about gene function with speculation about adaptive value

claim: Cellular quiescence allows for genetic variation.
source: Taken together, we conclude that cellular quiescence allows for genetic variation.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the phenotypic and genomic data
